function.name: generate_report
function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

**Ionisation methods – a quick guide** | Ionisation technique | Typical application | Key advantages | Common limitations | |----------------------|---------------------|----------------|--------------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Gas‑phase mass spectrometry (GC‑MS) | • Simple, robust;
• Produces reproducible fragmentation patterns;
• Good for volatile, thermally stable compounds | • Requires vacuum;
• Not suitable for large, labile molecules | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | GC‑MS, some LC‑MS | • Softer than EI → less fragmentation;
• Useful for larger, polar molecules | • Still needs GC‑compatible analytes;
• Lower sensitivity for very polar species | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | LC‑MS, especially for non‑polar to moderately polar analytes | • Operates at atmospheric pressure → minimal sample prep;
• Good for small molecules, drugs, lipids | • Less effective for highly polar or large biomolecules | | **Electrospray Ionisation (ESI)** | LC‑MS, proteomics, metabolomics | • Very soft → preserves intact ions;
• Handles large biomolecules (proteins, nucleic acids);
• Compatible with aqueous solutions | • Requires high‑pH or organic solvents for optimal ionisation;
• Suppression by salts or high‑concentration matrices | | **Matrix‑Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Proteomics, polymers, large biomolecules | • Rapid analysis;
• Minimal sample prep;
• Handles very large molecules (up to >1 MDa) | • Requires matrix;
• Limited for very small molecules;
• Ion suppression by contaminants | | **Photoionisation (PI)** | GC‑MS, LC‑MS, environmental analysis | • Non‑destructive, soft ionisation;
• Good for aromatic, UV‑absorbing compounds | • Requires UV‑active analytes;
• Lower sensitivity for non‑UV‑absorbing species | | **Laser Ablation Ionisation (LAI)** | Solid samples, surface analysis | • Direct sampling of solids;
• Minimal sample prep | • Requires laser system;
• Limited to surface‑accessible analytes | | **Field‑Ionisation (FII)** | High‑resolution MS, small molecules | • Ultra‑soft, minimal fragmentation | • Requires high vacuum and specialized equipment | --- ### How to choose the “best” method | Consideration | Recommended technique | |---------------|-----------------------| | **Sample state** (gas, liquid, solid) | Gas → EI/CI/PI; Liquid → ESI/APCI; Solid → MALDI/LAI | | **Molecular size** | Small (<500 Da) → EI/CI/APCI/PI; Medium (500–2000 Da) → ESI/APCI; Large (>2000 Da) → MALDI/ESI | | **Polarity** | Polar → ESI/APCI; Non‑polar → EI/CI | | **Desired fragmentation** | Detailed structural info → EI; Minimal fragmentation → CI/ESI/APCI | | **Speed & throughput** | Rapid screening → EI/ESI; High‑throughput LC‑MS → ESI/APCI | | **Matrix or solvent compatibility** | Aqueous or high‑salt samples → ESI; Organic solvents → APCI | | **Instrumentation cost & complexity** | Budget constraints → EI/CI; Advanced labs → MALDI/ESI | --- ### Quick decision tree 1. **Is the analyte volatile?** - **Yes** → Use **EI** (GC‑MS). - **No** → Go to 2. 2. **Is the analyte large (protein, peptide, polymer)?** - **Yes** → Use **MALDI** (solid‑phase) or **ESI** (LC‑MS). - **No** → Go to 3. 3. **Is the analyte polar or aqueous?** - **Yes** → Use **ESI** (LC‑MS). - **No** → Use **APCI** (LC‑MS) or **CI** (GC‑MS). --- ### Bottom line - **For routine small‑molecule analysis**: **EI** (GC‑MS) or **ESI/APCI** (LC‑MS). - **For large biomolecules**: **ESI** (LC‑MS) or **MALDI** (solid‑phase). - **For non‑polar, thermally stable gases**: **EI**. - **For polar, thermally labile liquids**: **ESI** or **APCI**. If you have a specific analyte or application in mind, let me know and I can narrow down the recommendation further!
